title: Lhuan-dre Pretorius Century Hands San Francisco Unicorns Decisive Victory Over MI New York
text:
Lhuan-dre Pretorius Century Hands San Francisco Unicorns Decisive Victory Over MI New York
San Francisco Unicorns 146-1 Defeats MI New York 143-9 by 9 Wickets
The first match back at Grand Prairie Stadium outside of Dallas, Texas is the return fixture from the last match played in Pomona.
The game would almost be a repeat of the game Sunday with one lone exception, Lhuan-dre Pretorius maiden T20 century would see San Francisco Unicorns net run rate sky rocket as they would pick up an easy 9 wicket win to put their first foot near a guaranteed postseason spot.
Ryan Rickelton and Sunny Patel Drag MI New York Over 140
MI New York would open with Ryan Rickelton and Quinton de Kock, de Kock going in the 3rd over on a reverse sweep gone wrong, a line drive going right to Hassan Khan from the bowling of captain Matthew Short. De Kock’s 6 from 7 deliveries wouldn’t be the only wicket Short would get in the power play, Monack Patel bowled onto the middle stump for only 1 in the 5th over. Despite those wickets, 8 boundaries between Rickelton, Nicholas Pooran and de Kock being enough to see the power play end 50-2.
Ryan Rickelton’s innings would end on 35 an over later, Matthew Short getting the opener to chop a delivery onto his own stumps. Short would bowl a captain’s innings with the ball, 4 overs delivered before drinks, 3 wickets for only 24 runs with 15 of his deliveries being dot ball.
The first over after drinks would see the wicket of Kieron Pollard (16) go, Anirudh Immanuel getting Pollard to chop onto his stumps 2nd ball after opening the 11th over for 6. Brody Couch would get Pooran (19) in the 12th on a ball that was initially ruled wide, Lhuan-dre Pretorius convinced of an edge. Upon review ultraedge confirmed contact with the bat.
Sunny Patel and Corey Anderson would put up a 6th wicket partnership of 43 runs before Anderson would be caught at deep backward square by Hammad Azam. From there the wickets would fall fast, Sunny Patel would go the in the same over as Corey Anderson to Matthew Short on the cover. Sunny Patel’s 32 from 23 would help MI New York end their innings at a well below par for Grand Prairie 143-9.
Lhuan-dre Pretorius Unbeaten Century Batters MI New York Bowling
It was almost unfair.
The power play from Lhuan-dre Pretorius and Finn Allen was as sensible as a power play could be chasing a target that was about 20-25 runs below par. Neither player took a risk with the bat and punished the ball when given the chance. When they didn’t hit a boundary, the pair rotated with ease as they got to 52 without loss after the opening 6.
The only MI New York highlight in the chase would come in the 7th over when Romario Shepherd would get Finn Allen to mistime a slog six, a ball that went right to Ryan Rickelton to see his innings end on 20. Matthew Short would dot the remaining deliveries for a wicket maiden, Shepherd’s third this MLC campaign.
But this chase was all about the poise a young 20 year old Pretorius had at the crease. He didn’t put a shot wrong and Matthew Short was more than happy to rotate back to Pretorius when he was on strike. Both decided the 13th over would be go time, Pretorius bringing up the 50 partnership from just 40 deliveries with a 6 over the seats.
Pretorius wouldn’t miss from here, a 15th over that saw 4 boundaries to get him close to the century. Pretorius would pick up a 52 ball century to close the contest out an over later, a six bringing him to 98, winning it with a four next ball to win by 9 wickets with 26 balls to spare.
One thing that has been remarkable to see as this MLC campaign has played out is seeing the growth from the Unicorns opener. He’s setting himself up to be a long standing fixture in the South African squad, and a headache for everyone he faces at the crease.
